objective: Present the selected release window and five production-baseline metrics in a stable two-level responsive summary without changing business behavior.
users: Configuration-management users reviewing the selected production window and baseline counts

requirements.statement: The selected release window must occupy a dedicated top information row with code, name and status.
acceptance: Window context is visually separate from metrics
Code, name and status remain readable on desktop
requirements.source: User selected option 2 and confirmed implementation on 2026-08-20.
counterexample: Window code remains one of six competing metric cells
Window name or status is omitted

requirements.statement: The five numeric metrics must render as one equal-width desktop row without an orphaned second row.
acceptance: All five metric cells share one row at desktop width
requirements.source: Layout defect visible in the user screenshot.
counterexample: Metric columns have visibly inconsistent widths

requirements.statement: The summary must adapt to two metric columns on narrow screens and one column on phone widths without overflow.
acceptance: Labels and values do not overlap at responsive breakpoints
counterexample: Borders or content overlap after wrapping

requirements.statement: The change must preserve existing selection, statistics, permissions and API behavior.
acceptance: No state, event or API contract changes
counterexample: Metric values or filtering behavior change
Backend or API changes are introduced

invariants: Existing selectedWindow and summary data remain authoritative
Existing design tokens and compact operational style are retained
constraints: Limit implementation to ReleaseBaselineView.vue and release-prototype.css
non_goals: Redesign the baseline toolbar or table

selected_approach.name: Window information row plus five-metric row
selected_approach.reason: It separates business context from outcome metrics and removes the existing five-track/six-item mismatch.

alternatives.name: Six cells in one row
alternatives.rejected_because: It fixes wrapping but preserves weak hierarchy between window context and metrics.

alternatives.name: Auto-fit metric cards
alternatives.rejected_because: Intermediate-width wrapping would be less predictable for a fixed metric set.

components.name: ReleaseBaselineView
components.responsibility: Render existing window context and metrics in two semantic layers.

components.name: release-prototype.css
components.responsibility: Provide stable desktop and responsive layout, spacing and separators.

interfaces.name: Baseline summary view model
interfaces.contract: selectedWindow and summary values are presented without transformation changes.

data_flows.input: Existing selected window and five summary counts

error_handling.behavior: Do not render the summary container.
error_handling.recovery: Summary appears when a window is selected.

error_handling.condition: Window name is longer than available space
error_handling.behavior: Keep the code and status visible while auxiliary text truncates safely.

performance: Static markup and CSS add no meaningful runtime cost
compatibility: No state, API, database or persisted-data changes

verification_strategy.signal: Desktop summary has a dedicated window row and one equal five-metric row.
verification_strategy.method: Browser screenshot and DOM layout inspection at desktop width.

verification_strategy.signal: Narrow and phone widths wrap predictably without overflow or overlap.
verification_strategy.method: Responsive screenshots and scrollWidth/clientWidth checks near 760px and 430px.

verification_strategy.signal: Existing behavior and type contracts remain valid.
verification_strategy.method: Production frontend build and scoped diff inspection.

assumptions.text: The red-boxed issue is the summary grid mismatch and weak information hierarchy.
assumptions.basis: The screenshot highlights only the malformed summary area and the user chose the hierarchical option.
assumptions.falsifier: The user requests different metrics, interactions or business semantics.

decisions.decision: Use a dedicated top window row and a lower five-metric row.
decisions.reason: It provides stronger hierarchy and stable alignment.

decisions.decision: Keep both layers inside one bordered summary container.
decisions.reason: It avoids nested cards and remains consistent with the operational UI.

decisions.decision: Use five desktop columns, two narrow columns and one phone column.
decisions.reason: The fixed metric set remains predictable at each breakpoint.

risks.risk: Long window names can compete with the status tag.
risks.mitigation: Use a shrinkable text area with ellipsis and a non-shrinking status tag.

risks.risk: Wrapped metric borders can look inconsistent at breakpoints.
risks.impact: Visual seams can appear between rows.
risks.mitigation: Define breakpoint-specific column and border rules and verify screenshots.

approval.evidence: The user selected option 2 and explicitly replied '确认并实施' on 2026-08-20.
